rv.q: Like a spinning disco ball, “Mary Gets Hers” bewitches the gaze.
Mary Gets Hers is wacky and winking, big on slapstick-and-clown-inspired physicality and, when it’s at its best, totally charming in its quirkification of Hrotsvitha’s dramatis personae.
"Mary Gets Hers" is clearly helmed by a clever creative team – and even an erudite one.
As it stands, Mary Gets Hers is instead a production worth seeing for the achievements of its other characters.
But in Mary Gets Hers, because Mary remains largely opaque, the language can start to feel as pop-culture slick as its view of female empowerment.
Alas, the buzzing troupe "putting on a play" may prove more amused tonight than its audience.
Instead, Mary Gets Hers — the title carrying its own ironic threat — merely registers as a series of silly sketches during which five players are encouraged to overact and gladly meet the challenge.
Unfortunately, it is not funny though the actors cheerfully mug their way through Horwitz’s text as though they find it hilarious.
Mary may get hers, but you’ll probably just get a headache.
The fun this terrific ensemble is having presenting this 10th century story is infectious and the silliness of it all is a joy to be part of.
But judging by the sparse laughter from the audience, Mary Gets Hers is more of a groaner than mood-elevator.

cn.t: Horwitz's irreverent medieval adaptation divides critics with its quirky humor and inventive staging. Some praise its spiky adventurousness and charm, while others find it overly cutesy and less funny than it thinks it is.
